found_values.value: The one input a panel setting picks fills the BENCH rpm register and feeds the motor stall action. The panel already enables and places a rotation input by setting (SET_OPTICAL_EN 'Once per revolution, gives the phase', SET_OPTICAL_PIN 'GPIO'), and the BENCH page carries one rpm register (LINK_BN_RPM = 3) with one valid bit (LINK_BN_RPM_OK = 1u << 2). Each rotation input has its own front end and GPIO (Pins.md), none multiplexed, so any one can be picked. Derived from the tree

65,535 rpm: the highest speed the BENCH rpm register carries (to_u16 saturates at 65,535 counts of 1 rpm) and the speed V225, V290 and V292 compute at. A once-per-revolution input and the vibration fundamental reach 1,092.25 Hz; the phase-wire clip, which reads the electrical frequency (V293), reaches 22,937 Hz at 21 pole pairs (MOTOR_POLES even, 2 to 42). A commercial stand's electrical probe reads 0 to 190k eRPM ('Angular speed* 0 190k 1 eRPM')
found_values.source: checkout 4e10669ebcff: shared/bench/bench_state.c:21-28; hardware/docs/Research.md:929 (V225), :994 (V290), :996 (V292), :997 (V293); https://cdn.rcbenchmark.com/landing_pages/Manuals/Series%201585%20Datasheet.pdf, extracted text line 89 (vendors.py fetch, HTTP 200)

found_values.value: 10 rpm, read by at least one of the optical index, the magnetic pickup or the encoder, the coast-down after a disarm included. The phase-wire clip is not required below 500 rpm: the Series 1585 datasheet states its optical probe measures 'speeds from 10 to 30,000 RPM' and that 'the electrical RPM probe does not work effectively when the motor is running at low RPM (<500)'

120 V at the clip's input, taken by the divider and clamp that stage 2 selects; the comparator sees only the divided signal. The phase node switches between the ESC pack's negative and positive nodes, so its peak follows the pack node. No primary source states a motor phase's overshoot. FU-2A's R3 P2 derives a plug-in ring of the pack node of 117 to 120 V with little series resistance ('With little series resistance the plug-in ring reaches 117 V to 120 V'), and selection.json holds no part for 'pack overvoltage and transient clamp'. Derived, not measured

found_values.value: A Hall-effect bipolar latch with a digital open-drain output, which R11 selects, on a sensor board of its own that JLCPCB assembles, supplied at 3.3 V from the IO board's logic rail; its output is pulled up to 3.3 V on the IO board into measurement GPIO 27. A latch switches on a south pole and holds until a north pole ('The absence of a magnetic field causes the output to continue to drive the current state'), which V218's two opposite magnets present once a turn
found_values.source: DRV5015 data sheet SBAS915A, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/drv5015.pdf (vendors.py fetch, HTTP 200), sections 1, 5, 6.3, 7.1; checkout 4e10669ebcff hardware/docs/Pins.md:124 (GPIO 27, magnetic pickup)

found_values.value: One pulse per revolution, from two equal magnets of opposite polarity fixed 180 degrees apart on the bell, which add no static unbalance as far as their masses and radii match ('Anything attached to the bell is mass on the part being balanced'). Reading the rotor's poles (MOTOR_POLES / 2 pulses, up to 21) puts the latch at 22,937 Hz at 65,535 rpm, above the 20 kHz minimum sensing bandwidth of DRV5015 and AH1711; one pulse a turn is 1,092 Hz, and the reading does not use MOTOR_POLES

found_values.value: 5 mm: the sensor's stated operating range includes 5 mm. The maker of a commercial stand gives the probe-to-motor distance for its Series 1520, 1580 and 1585 probe as 'It needs to be less than 5mm'. Those probes read reflective tape; the bench's mark is a pen line (docs/Balance.md:36), whose width and reflectance are not stated

On a sensor board of its own that JLCPCB assembles, with parts that carry LCSC numbers under the IO board's sourcing rules, connected by the lead of V222 (2 m at most). The board carries the accelerometer, its CX and CY capacitors (4.7 nF or more, V225) and the lead buffer (function 'accelerometer lead buffer'). Every analogue accelerometer read is a surface-mount package that needs a board: LFCSP-12 4 x 4 mm (ADXL316), LFCSP-16 4 x 4 mm (ADXL326), LCC-8 5 x 5 mm (AD22035Z)

The single-ended form reads 5 V logic (F4), and every line input withstands 12 V without damage, the supply the second jumper can put on the encoder: an encoder whose push-pull outputs swing to its supply, or the jumper at 12 V with a 5 V encoder, puts up to 12 V on the signal pins. Derived from F4

8 to 288 kHz of ESC PWM, wider than the 24, 48 and 96 kHz the programmer screen offers. AM32 takes a PWM frequency setting from 8 to 144 kHz ('if (eepromBuffer.pwm_frequency < 145 && eepromBuffer.pwm_frequency > 7)', 'TIMER1_MAX_ARR = TIM1_AUTORELOAD * 400 / divider'), and its variable-PWM mode 1 maps the auto-reload between TIMER1_MAX_ARR / 2 and TIMER1_MAX_ARR, up to twice the setting. The clip passes up to 22,937 Hz, which overlaps an 8 kHz PWM

found_values.value: 1.244 us of delay variation at 1,092.25 Hz (65,535 rpm) for the optical index: the sensor, its front end and the index comparator together, where the delay variation is the drift of one unit between runs and each unit's fixed delay, its unit-to-unit spread included, cancels in the trial run (V225, owner 2026-10-02). 1 degree of the 915.54 us period is 2.543 us for the whole chain (V225); R10's share is 52 ns (V290, V291); the accelerometer and the optical index take 1.244 us each. In angle that is 0.489 degree at every speed: at 10,000 rpm the split gives 8.16 us each

requirements.value: the fundamental from 16.7 Hz (1,000 rpm) to 1,092 Hz (65,535 rpm) reaches the output with the sensor's resonance above 1,092 Hz; the RFILT x CX pole's fixed attenuation at a given speed cancels in the trial run as its fixed delay does

requirements.name: balance resolution
requirements.value: 1 mg at the fundamental after one run's 5 s of averaging: noise in the 0.2 Hz band of a 5 s record under 1 mg

requirements.name: static angle resolution
requirements.value: 0.1 degree on 2 axes, DC-coupled, zeroed on a reference surface: sin(0.1 deg) x 1 g = 1.75 mg

requirements.name: filter capacitor
requirements.value: CX and CY at 4.7 nF or more, the data sheets' recommended minimum

requirements.name: delay drift between runs
requirements.value: the drift of one unit's delay between the runs of a balance at most 1.244 us at 1,092 Hz (0.489 degree at every speed) for the sensor, its RFILT x CX pole and the lead buffer together; each unit's fixed delay and its unit-to-unit spread cancel. For a single pole the phase moves by (dRC/RC) x x / (1 + x^2) rad, x = 2 pi f RC, at most half the fractional change of RFILT x CX where the pole sits inside 16.7 to 1,092 Hz, which every CX of 4.7 nF or more puts it: RFILT x CX may change by at most 1.71 % between runs, plus a stated bound on the sensor's own response

requirements.name: lead length
requirements.value: drives the input of the lead buffer on the sensor board (function 'accelerometer lead buffer'), so the capacitance of the lead of up to 2 m stays off the RFILT x CX node

report.value: No accelerometer shows the 1.244 us share under V225's ruling of 2026-10-02. The fixed delay of the RFILT x CX pole and its unit-to-unit spread now cancel: at CX = 4.7 nF ADXL316WBCSZ's pole sits at 915 to 1,254 Hz and delays 1,092 Hz by 104.40 to 127.26 us, the 22.86 us spread that failed FU-2D. What counts is the drift of one unit between runs. For a single pole the phase moves by (dRC/RC) x x / (1 + x^2) rad, x = 2 pi f RC; the share is 0.489 degree at every speed (1.244 us at 1,092 Hz, 8.16 us at 10,000 rpm), so where the pole sits inside 16.7 to 1,092 Hz, as every CX of 4.7 nF or more puts it, RFILT x CX may change by at most 1.71 % between runs (1.708 % at 32 kOhm; 72.8 us of delay per unit fractional change at 1,092 Hz). With a C0G CX the drift is RFILT's. ADXL316 Rev. C, ADXL326 Rev. 0 and the ADXL103/ADXL203 data sheet Rev. F (AD22035Z) state RFILT's tolerance (27 to 37 kOhm; 32 kOhm +/-15 %; 24 to 40 kOhm) but no temperature coefficient of RFILT and no phase or bandwidth over temperature; the sensor's own response (resonance 4.2 kHz typical for ADXL316, 5.5 kHz for AD22035) has no drift figure either; and the temperature change at the sensor between runs is not stated. ADXL316WBCSZ (JLCPCB 104) and AD22035Z (JLCPCB 83) pass every other value, rule 4 and the lead length with the buffer. The accelerometer keeps no part: its fit is not known until RFILT's drift is stated by the maker or measured

At the IO board end the ADCS7476's sampling needs a series resistor and a reservoir capacitor (stage 2 passives): an RC of time constant tau adds about tau of delay at 1,092 Hz and drifts by tau times the fractional drift of R x C, for example 11 ns for tau = 110 ns and a 10 % change. data.function: P2 report: encoder decode resources for P5
data.ruling: The refutation stands on its first point. The figure gives "clk_sys at least 75 MHz for 5 MHz a channel at 40/60 duty" as the floor P5 reserves. The function's own requirement in P2's tables (FU-2C and FU-2D, "edge spacing tolerated") is at least 32 ns of A-to-B spacing at 5 MHz, at 40, 50 and 60 % duty with 3 ns jitter. That is the spacing the AM26LV32EIDR leaves: 50 - (26 - 8) = 32 ns, from SLLS849E 6.6. At 75 MHz, P2's unchanged model fails that requirement. The arithmetic 6 cycles in 80 ns = 75 MHz is correct but bounds only the same-channel edge path. The binding limit is the other channel's level, which JMP PIN reads about 2 cycles after the synchroniser. That limit is about 26.7 ns at 75 MHz and leaves no margin at 32 ns minus 3 ns of jitter. Without reversals, the model's floor at 32 ns and 3 ns jitter is about 77 to 80 MHz, not 75 MHz. At P2's own phase settings (40 ns at 40 %, 50 ns at 60 %), 75 MHz passes. So the figure holds only for spacings wider than the function requires. The 150 MHz default is unaffected: every case decodes there. Second point: 19 of 32 words is correct only when both state machines share one loaded copy. The tree's per-binding loading (out_dshot.c:88, pio_add_program per output; Research.md P5 row) would need 38 words, which do not fit in one block. The figure leaves this out. P5 should state it, but on its own it does not falsify a value. Results with 100 reversals are not used. At those clocks they fail even at 80 to 100 MHz, because the model reverses instantly at full rate, which is not a physical waveform at 5 MHz.

data.function: re-rank report: lead buffer output span
data.ruling: The refutation stands. The figure gives the ADXL316 span as 0.45 to 2.95 V at VS 3.399 V. That span does not follow from the limits the figure itself states. The span 0.449 to 2.950 V comes only from an ideal 0 g level of 0.5 x VS with 16 g at 23 mV/V/g. With the stated 0 g band of 0.4 to 0.6 x VS (Table 1: 1.2 to 1.8 V at VS 3 V, ratiometric), the worst-case span at VS 3.399 V is 0.109 to 3.290 V. The figure therefore understates the span by about 0.34 V at each end. A figure that the re-rank reports for the buffer's output span has to state the correct span, so it is refuted as written. The scope is the function: the error is in this function's requirement arithmetic, not in any part. The conclusion the figure draws, that output swing does not separate the candidates, is not overturned. The sensor's own output limits its signal, at typical 0.1 V low and 2.8 V high (no load, VS 3 V; about VS - 0.2 V at 3.399 V, if that scales). The sensor's swing values are typical only, not guaranteed. That is inside the 10 to 20 mV rail margin the two buffer datasheets I re-read give at 10 kOhm. For the re-rank, the corrected figure is: 0.11 to 3.29 V from the 0 g and scale factor limits, held to about 0.1 to about 3.2 V (typical) by the sensor's output swing. Not re-read here: MCP6022 and the other candidates' swing. The TLV9062 and OPA365 rows are given at VS 5.5 V, not at 3.3 V.
